name: Telescope Array
summary: Hybrid ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray observatory in Utah, USA, combining a surface scintillator array and fluorescence telescopes. The collaboration's diffuse and point-source ultrahigh-energy-photon searches test models including superheavy dark-matter decay.
physics_targets: Ultrahigh-energy photons from superheavy dark-matter decay
detection_principle: Measures ground particles and atmospheric fluorescence from extensive air showers. Photon analyses combine 16 reconstructed observables, including shower-front curvature, lateral distributions and waveform timing, in a multivariate classifier, then estimate hadronic backgrounds to set photon-flux limits.
technologies: Solar power and wireless data acquisition

sites.name: Utah West Desert / Delta
sites.location: Western Utah desert near Delta, USA

status.label: Official page describes observations; the status page is undated
status.evidence: The ICRR mission website describes cosmic-ray observations in Utah. Its 2026 news mainly concerns recruitment, so those dates are not treated as evidence of continuous data taking.

timeline.event: The baseline array began full hybrid observations; the surface-array paper separately describes SD operation from May 2008.
Published diffuse-photon limits from nine years of data.
Published northern-sky photon point-source search results.

collaboration.name: Telescope Array Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: The ICRR website lists international participation from Japan, the United States, Russia, South Korea and Belgium; membership should follow authorship for each phase.

key_parameters.name: Original surface array used in the photon analyses in this dossier
key_parameters.value: 507 stations; 3 m² of plastic scintillator per station; about 700 km², with 1.2 km spacing

key_parameters.name: Typical photon-search thresholds
key_parameters.value: Several integral thresholds from 10^18 eV to 10^20 eV; not a dark-matter mass range

phases.name: Original TA hybrid array
phases.description: The parameters and photon papers in this dossier mainly refer to this configuration.

phases.name: TALE / TAx4 extensions and expansion
phases.description: Retained as aliases within the same project series. Completion of individual expansion components in 2026 was not rechecked; the original 507 stations cannot be treated as the total present facility.

results.summary: The nine-year surface-array diffuse-photon search found two candidates, compatible with expected background. The 95% CL integral flux limit above 10^18 eV is 0.067 km^-2 yr^-1 sr^-1.

No significant photon point source was found in the northern-sky search. Above 10^18 eV, the direction-averaged 95% CL point-source flux limit is 0.094 km^-2 yr^-1; see the paper for other thresholds.

science_scope: The collaboration's photon searches test superheavy-dark-matter models and constitute indirect detection. Their limits also test conventional cosmic-ray sources and cosmogenic photons; individual ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray events cannot simply be labeled dark-matter candidates. TA and the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) are distinct projects.
